rationale: The buyer is an early-stage startup founder or developer who has real financial skin in the game (personal credit card being charged despite $25k GCP credits), making this a genuine acute pain rather than a theoretical one. Buyer clarity is moderate: startup founders using GCP for Startups is a nameable cohort reachable through YC/accelerator communities, but individual willingness to pay for a one-time audit/guide is uncertain — the pain is acute but episodic, and once resolved the customer has no reason to return. Operational autonomy is viable if the product is a self-serve guide or automated diagnostic, but needs validation that founders will pay rather than just Google the answer.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a Firebase/GCP billing migration checklist + automated billing-account diagnostic: a step-by-step guide that walks startup founders through verifying their Firebase project is correctly linked to their startup billing account and that credits are applied, plus a simple web form where they input their project ID and get back a Claude-generated diagnostic report. The factory builds this as a Claude prompt that interprets pasted GCP billing screenshots or exported billing data, wrapped in a minimal form page (Typeform or similar) with a Stripe payment link ($29-49 one-time). To sell, the factory drafts posts/replies in relevant communities (HN, Reddit r/googlecloud, GCP for Startups Slack, YC alumni networks) pointing to the tool — Youval approves each post before it goes live. Delivery is instant (automated report emailed on payment), support is Claude-answered FAQ, and billing is Stripe. The only recurring operator touch is approving community posts and reviewing any edge-case support tickets Claude flags. Key risk: this pain is episodic (one-time per startup migration), so LTV is low and the market needs volume to work — validate that enough founders hit this problem monthly before investing further.
notes: total 5.5 exactly meets the validate threshold. Pain is episodic (low pain_frequency at 4) which limits LTV; validate whether the GCP for Startups program generates enough monthly new entrants to sustain volume. Defensibility is low (3) — easily copied — so speed to validate matters.
